activities.title: Average speed over an interval
activities.lede: Synthetic test data: the table records cumulative distance travelled, measured from the start. It is not a displacement table.

examples.label: Average speed over an interval
examples.prompt: Use the measurements to find the average speed over the full interval from 0 s to 4 s.

steps.math:
Total distance = 12 m
Elapsed time = 4 s − 0 s = 4 s
steps.text: Read the final cumulative distance and subtract the start time from the end time.

steps.math: Average speed = total distance ÷ elapsed time
steps.text: Average speed uses total distance travelled. Average velocity instead uses displacement and includes direction.
Substitute the measured distance and elapsed time. Metres divided by seconds gives metres per second.

Over these four seconds, the object covered an average of 3 metres per second. The samples show equal distance increments in each one-second interval; they do not establish what happened between observations.
steps.note: An overall average does not prove constant instantaneous speed.

questions.stem: What do the sampled measurements establish about each one-second interval, and what remains unknown about motion between observations? Explain why this distance table cannot determine the direction of average velocity.
